Maya (design): Putting up a small follow-up thread for the compact invocation preview. Goal: make run history denser while keeping structured outputs discoverable. Attached prototype: https://figma.redwood/playground-compact-invoke-v2

Diego (eng): Looks promising. Two implementation asks: 1) collapse args/results by default, 2) provide a stable card height in the list to avoid jank while lazy-loading images/avatars.

Samira (devex): +1. Also calling out inconsistent verbs: sometimes we have 'Run' (prompt), 'Execute' (tools), 'Invoke' (tool docs). I'd prefer standardizing on 'Invoke' for tool-level actions in the Playground.

Jules (a11y): Accessibility checklist: card should expose role="article" with aria-label="Tool name, invocation status, timestamp"; the expand toggle must have aria-expanded and a clear accessible name. Use aria-live="polite" for dynamic result snippets.

Maya (design): Good checklist. UX question: when summarizing structured output, do we surface a generated natural-language line (e.g. "Invoice draft (id:123) \u2014 ok") or render selected key/value chips inline? Which scales better visually?

Diego (eng): For performance and parsing complexity, single-line generated summary is easiest. We can build a tiny summary formatter in the backend that returns a human-friendly string. Key/value chips might be expensive for long records.

Samira (devex): If we go with a summary string, it should prioritize human-readable fields: title/name, then status, then id. Also add a small JSON icon that opens a detailed inspector. The inspector can be an inline drawer to avoid blocking context.

Jules (a11y): Inline drawer is fine but ensure focus management: when opened, focus moves into the drawer and the drawer has role="region" and aria-label="Full invocation output". When closed, focus returns to the toggle. Also provide a skip link to jump straight to full output for keyboard users.

Maya (design): Copy options for summary ordering: A) "ok \u2014 Invoice draft (id: 123)" B) "Invoice draft (id: 123) \u2014 ok". Which reads better in a dense timeline?

Diego (eng): Option B. Sorting and search will likely surface by title, so put title first. Makes scan faster.

Samira (devex): UI density note: our dense history rows use 12px meta today which fails contrast checks in dark mode. Propose bumping to 13-14px and increasing foreground contrast token. Also ensure line-height >= 1.2 so truncation doesn't cut off glyphs.

Jules (a11y): Agree. Also request we test with screen magnification and VoiceOver to ensure truncated content is still announced fully in the accessible name.

Maya (design): Action labels: change contextual menu item from 'Show full output' to 'View full output' to align with microcopy guide. Primary button on the card becomes 'Invoke'. Secondary menu has 'View full output'.

Diego (eng): For telemetry, we'll emit an event when the JSON inspector is opened (playground.invoke.output_viewed) with invocation id and model tag. Samira, ok to add to the PR checklist?

Samira (devex): Yes. I'll add telemetry, aria attributes, and the copy updates. Also will prototype both inline drawer and modal in the PR so QA can test focus/announcement behavior.

Maya (design): Thanks team. I'll post updated Figma frames and a short notes doc with the summary formatter rules. Will follow up on any edge-case keys that should be surfaced in the one-line summary. :sparkles:
